public_rationale: The evidence supports the claim of intensifying AI backlash in its US context [e1, e2, e3]. Gallup's May 4–11, 2026 survey of US adults found that 39% believed AI did more harm than good, up from 31% in 2025; the results were published July 28 [e1]. Data Center Watch reported that active data-center opposition groups more than doubled between the end of 2025 and January–March 2026, reaching 49 states [e2]. It recorded at least 75 projects worth approximately $130 billion blocked or delayed by local opposition that quarter [e2]. June 13 reporting identified electricity costs, water use and noise among residents' concerns [e3]. Together, these findings show worsening general sentiment and expanding organized infrastructure opposition with observable consequences across several concerns [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: The evidence supplies no common numerical measure of 'really intense.'
Data-center opposition over local impacts does not establish opposition to AI generally [e2, e3].
Gallup's fieldwork falls within the target period, but publication followed the June 26 statement [e1].

Worldwide intensification is not established. Public First reports more positive attitudes in emerging economies and Asian countries, but unspecified fieldwork dates limit its relevance to the January–June 2026 period [e4].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Public backlash against AI is getting really intense.

statement.excerpt: • Backlash against AI is getting really intense for many reasons
statement.document_title: The month Generative AI lost its mojo

our_interpretation: The plain reading is substantially growing negative sentiment and organized opposition, rather than universal rejection of AI.
The surrounding US-focused discussion makes American public opinion and opposition central, while evidence from elsewhere tests the breadth of that reading.
Because no reporting period is named, use the first half of 2026 through the post date, with earlier observations as trend baselines.
Intensity requires evidence beyond isolated critical comments: worsening comparable polling or organized opposition with observable consequences.
For many reasons refers to multiple reported concerns, not a quantified causal claim.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence from the target period shows a substantial increase in negative sentiment and organized opposition across more than one concern or constituency.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence shows that negative sentiment and organized opposition were broadly stable or diminishing, with only isolated criticism.

evidence.locator: Opening summary; sections on harm, trust and jobs; Survey Methods
evidence.explanation: The May 4–11 survey found that Americans saying AI does more harm than good rose from 31% to 39% year over year; expected job losses also increased and trust declined. These changes support growing negative sentiment, though Gallup describes some shifts as modest.

The Q1 summary documents a substantial increase in organized opposition, alongside blocked or delayed projects. June 13 is the verified public-availability bound supplied by e3; the original summary page does not state its publication day.

evidence.locator: Second article paragraph; publication date above article
evidence.explanation: This contemporaneous article reports the Q1 disruption findings and identifies electricity costs, water use and noise among residents' concerns. It corroborates the timing and multiple-concern aspect, but is not independent of Data Center Watch's project counts.

The report describes worsening US and UK sentiment while finding substantially more positive attitudes in emerging economies and Asian countries. This limits any worldwide reading; its October 8 update and unspecified fieldwork dates prevent treating it as decisive evidence for the first-half window.
